newsitem.title: USA: Vermilion Bay gas pipelines shut for leak testing.
newsitem.headline: Vermilion Bay gas pipelines shut for leak testing.

text.p: Natural gas pipelines lacing Louisiana's Vermilion Bay were ordered shut for testing on Thursday after a leak was spotted on the inland waters, the U.S. Coast Guard and Louisiana officials said.
"Bubbles have been spotted, but they are small bubbles and there is no sheen," a Coast Guard spokesman told Reuters.

Testing could take several hours as the pipelines, which include a handful of larger interstate pipelines and dozens of gathering lines, are bleeded down and pressure tested, a state pipeline official said.
"I think they are closing that down right now. The lines are being shut off and will bleed down" said Mariano Hinojosa, pipeline director with the Louisiana Office of Conservation.
"They understand what (is leaking) and where it is. Now they've got to find out who it is," he said.

Acadian Gas Pipeline, Louisiana Resources Co, Sea Robin Pipeline and Texas Gas Transmission Corp each operate major pipelines running through the bay waters about 40 miles south of Lafayette, La., he said.
"It is a congested area of pipes and wells and flow lines," Hinojosa said.
Capacity of those pipelines was not immediately available.
